title: CSEval: Towards Automated, Multi-Dimensional, and Reference-Free Counterspeech Evaluation using Auto-Calibrated LLMs
measurement_description: The paper measures the quality of automatically generated counterspeech against religious hate speech, specifically focusing on evaluating responses to anti-Muslim stereotypes and Islamophobia. It assesses whether a counterspeech effectively refutes the religious bias, stereotype, or prejudice expressed in the original hate speech.
findings: The paper finds that traditional, similarity-based evaluation metrics (like ROUGE, METEOR) are ineffective at assessing the quality of counterspeech for nuanced topics like religious hate speech. These metrics often score a less relevant counterspeech higher than a more effective one that directly addresses the underlying religious stereotype (e.g., Islamophobia). The proposed LLM-based, multi-dimensional evaluation framework (Auto-CSEval) aligns more closely with human judgment, successfully identifying and scoring higher the counterspeech that more effectively refutes religious bigotry.
